la:noun:squalor.html:
squālor, ōris, m.
Sanscr. kālas, black; Gr. κελαινός, κηλίς
.
In gen., stiffness, roughness: quaecumque (res) aspera constat, Non aliquo sine materiae squalore reperta est (opp. lēvor),.—
In partic., stiffness from dirt, dirtiness, filthiness, foulness, squalor (the predom. signif. of the word; syn.: sordes, illuvies).
Lit.
In gen.: immundas fortunas aequum est squalorem sequi,: squaloris plenus ac pulveris (opp. unguentis oblitus),: obsita erat squalore vestis,: illuvie, squalore enecti,: ignavis et imbellibus manet squalor (corresp. to crinem barbamque submittere),: senex macie et squalore confectus,: vitis squalore deciso,,

14, 39, § 138: squalore situque posito,.—

Esp., of places: locorum squalor et solitudines inviae militem terrebant,desolation,; cf.: silva squalore tenebrarum horrenda,.—
So esp. freq. of filthy garments, as a sign of mourning: decesserat ex Asiā frater meus magno squalore, sed multo majore maerore,: aspicite, judices, squalorem sordesque sociorum,; so (with sordes and luctus) ; ; ; ; ; Metell. ap. ; ; ; with maestitia,.—
Trop.: deterso rudis saeculi squalore,i. e. in language,: Gallus, ex squalore nimio miseriarum, ad principale culmen provectus,i. e. from the very lowest rank,.

la:verb:squaleo.html:
squālĕo, ŭi, 2, v. n.
squalor
,
to be stiff or rough with any thing, etc. (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; cf. sordeo).
Lit.
In gen.: squalentes infode conchas,i. e. rough,: per tunicam squalentem auro,; cf.: auro squalens lorica,: maculis auro squalentibus,; : picti squalentia terga lacerti,: squalentia tela venenis, .—
In partic.
To be stiff or rough from dryness or drought, to be dry, parched: squalebant pulvere fauces,: oraque projecta squalent arentia linguā,: tellus squalet,.—Hence,
Of lands, etc., to be desert, untilled, waste: squalentes campi,; : squalens litus,: squalentia arva Libyes,; : sterilis profundi vastitas squalet soli,.—
To be stiff or rough from slovenliness or want of care; to be filthy, neglected, squalid: squalenti Dido comā,: squalens barba,: crines squalent a pulvere effuso,: barba cruore,: vestes squalentes atro pulvere,: neque ego arma squalere situ ac rubigine velim, sed fulgorem inesse,; : mihi supellex squalet atque aedes meae,: invidiae nigro squalentia tabo Tecta petit,; cf. : squalent abductis arva colonis,lie untilled,; cf. 1. β, supra.—
Transf., to mourn in filthy or squalid garments (cf. sordes and sordidatus; in Cic. only so): erat in luctu senatus: squalebat civitas publico consilio mutatā veste,: luget senatus, maeret equester ordo, tota civitas confecta senio est, squalent municipia, afflictantur coloniae,. —P. a. as subst.: squālĕntĭa, ōrum, n., deserts, .
